chapters.summary: Isaiah 1 is the prophet's indictment and call to Judah and Jerusalem, exposing their rebellion and empty worship, and summoning them to repent with the promise of forgiveness and restoration.
keyPoints: God rebukes Israel's rebellion, like children turning against their father, when even the ox and donkey know their master.
God despises hollow sacrifices and religious ritual, and calls instead for genuine repentance and righteous living.
God calls sinners to wash and make themselves clean, promising forgiveness to those who listen, and judgment to those who refuse.
chapters.application: We should examine our own faith - are we caught up in outward form while neglecting an honest heart? God delights when we do justice and love mercy, and he is ready to forgive all who truly repent.

chapters.summary: Isaiah foresees the nations streaming to the LORD's mountain in the last days, and calls the house of Jacob to walk in the LORD's light, while warning that the proud will be brought low.
keyPoints: In the last days the LORD's house will be established, and all nations will stream to his mountain to learn his ways.
The LORD will judge among the nations, and swords will be beaten into plowshares, so that war is learned no more.
Because the land is filled with idols and pride, the day of the LORD's judgment will bring every proud person low.
chapters.application: Today let us humbly rely on the Lord, putting away the pride and idols in our hearts, walking in his light, and looking forward to a future of peace and righteousness.

chapters.summary: Isaiah declares the LORD's judgment on Jerusalem and Judah for their rebellion, which has brought social chaos and corrupt leadership, though a remnant remains and future restoration is promised.
keyPoints: God will take away the food, water, and leaders Judah has relied on, plunging society into chaos.
The people oppress one another, the young are insolent toward their elders, and the women live in extravagance and vanity, drawing God's punishment.
The righteous God will judge sin, yet the righteous will be kept safe, and Zion will one day be restored.
chapters.application: When society is full of injustice and pride, let us examine ourselves, turn away from extravagance and arrogance, and set our hearts wholly on God, for he watches over the righteous and will surely judge the wicked.

chapters.summary: Isaiah 4 pictures Jerusalem's restoration after judgment, and God's holy protection and glorious presence over the remnant.
keyPoints: Seven women take hold of one man and beg to bear his name, so ashamed are they - a picture of how war has left so few men.
The LORD washes away Zion's filth and cleanses her bloodstains with a spirit of burning, making the remnant holy.
God comes down on Mount Zion, covering it with cloud and fire, providing shelter and rest for his people.
chapters.application: However hard our circumstances, God promises to cleanse and protect his people. May we depend on his Spirit in daily life, pursue holiness, and trust that his presence brings peace and covering.

chapters.summary: This chapter uses the song of the vineyard as a parable for Israel's rebellion, and declares God's judgment and discipline.
keyPoints: God compares Israel to a vineyard, expecting justice but finding violence instead.
Six woes are pronounced, condemning pride, greed, drunken revelry, and other sins.
Judgment is prophesied to be near, and foreign enemies will destroy the rebellious people.
chapters.application: Examine whether your life is bearing the fruit of righteousness. Turn away from pride and greed, humble yourself before God, and answer his call with faith.

chapters.summary: Isaiah sees the glory of the Lord in the temple, is overwhelmed by his own uncleanness, is cleansed by God, and accepts his call, along with a prophecy of Israel's rebellion and coming restoration.
keyPoints: Isaiah sees the Lord seated on a high and lofty throne, the seraphim calling out 'Holy, holy, holy,' and the temple filled with smoke.
Isaiah is undone, confessing that his lips are unclean, until a seraph touches his mouth with a burning coal and his sin is taken away.
The Lord asks who will go, and Isaiah answers, 'Here am I; send me,' receiving his commission to preach.
chapters.application: When we feel unworthy or weak, remember that God is able to cleanse us and call us into his work. May we, like Isaiah, respond to his call and say, 'Here am I; send me.'

chapters.summary: Isaiah urges King Ahaz to trust God, prophesies the sign of Immanuel, and announces the judgment that Assyria will bring.
keyPoints: King Ahaz is terrified by the threat of the alliance between Syria and Ephraim.
Isaiah, sent by God, urges the king to be calm and trust the LORD rather than panic over his enemies' schemes.
God gives the sign of Immanuel, foreshadowing both the suffering Judah will face and the restoration to come.
chapters.application: When trouble comes, we should look in faith to God's promises rather than act out of raw instinct. God will guide us with his presence, giving us peace and hope.

chapters.summary: Isaiah 8 records how the prophet was commanded to write down his prophecy, warning Judah not to rely on Assyria but to trust God instead, and declaring that God, Immanuel, will be with his people.
keyPoints: God instructs Isaiah to write down the prophecy and to name his son Maher-shalal-hash-baz, a sign that Assyria will plunder swiftly.
Because Judah rejects the gently flowing waters of God, the mighty flood of the Assyrian army will sweep over them - yet God will be with those who fear him.
Isaiah teaches his disciples to wait for and rely on God; though darkness comes, a faint light still guides the way.
chapters.application: When circumstances look threatening, let us learn to rely wholly on God rather than on human schemes. He will be our sanctuary, guiding us through darkness and giving us peace and hope.

chapters.summary: Isaiah prophesies that the people walking in darkness will see a great light, for a child is born to us who will reign on David's throne with justice and righteousness forever.
keyPoints: God will bring glory to despised Galilee, the land of Zebulun and Naphtali, as a great light shines upon it.
The prophecy foretells the Messiah's birth and mission - he will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.
God's anger comes upon the people because of their pride and sin, yet mercy remains within the judgment, and salvation will ultimately be accomplished.
chapters.application: However dark the circumstances, remember that God has already given us Jesus as our light. Trust him, find peace and hope in hardship, and live out a life of righteousness and peace.

chapters.summary: This chapter announces God's judgment on the proud nation of Assyria, and promises that the remnant will return and rely on God without fear.
keyPoints: God uses Assyria as the rod of his judgment, but because Assyria's heart is proud, it too will be punished.
God has mercy on the remnant; though disciplined, they will ultimately return.
Assyria's pride will be broken like a forest cut down, but God will preserve a holy remnant.
chapters.application: When trouble comes, examine yourself and humbly rely on God, for he governs all things and will surely keep his people to the end.

chapters.summary: Isaiah prophesies that a shoot will come up from the root of Jesse, and the Messiah will rule with righteousness and faithfulness, bringing peace and harmony.
keyPoints: A shoot will come up from the root of Jesse - the Messiah will come from the line of David.
The Messiah, filled with the Spirit, will delight in the fear of the LORD and carry out righteous judgment.
His kingdom will bring harmony to all creation, with the wolf dwelling with the lamb, and the earth filled with the knowledge of the LORD.
chapters.application: In a chaotic world, let us look forward to Christ's return, wait in faith for that kingdom of peace, and live out righteousness and mercy today as children of peace.

chapters.summary: Isaiah 12 is a song of thanksgiving, prophesying God's promised salvation and declaring the joy and praise found in his deliverance.
keyPoints: God is our salvation and strength; those who trust him will not be afraid.
Drawing water joyfully from the wells of salvation pictures the life and comfort God gives.
God's mighty deeds are proclaimed among the nations, for he has done glorious things.
chapters.application: Whatever our circumstances, let us remember God's salvation, sing his praise with a thankful heart, rely on him in hardship, and share the joy of this salvation with others.

chapters.summary: Isaiah declares God's judgment on Babylon, foretelling its destruction, and emphasizes that the day of the LORD is near, revealing God's sovereignty and righteousness.
keyPoints: God gathers the nations to carry out judgment, and Babylon will be destroyed.
The day of the LORD draws near; hearts melt with fear and the heavens and earth are shaken.
Babylon's pride will be brought low, made like Sodom and Gomorrah.
chapters.application: When we face a world in turmoil and warnings of judgment, let us humbly repent, trust in God's righteousness and salvation, and live holy lives in hope.

chapters.summary: This chapter announces God's judgment on Babylon, foretelling that its pride will be brought low, while Israel will receive mercy and return home.
keyPoints: The LORD will have compassion on Jacob and again choose Israel, bringing them back to their own land.
Babylon's tyrant will finally be cut off and the whole earth will be at rest; a taunt song mocks his fall.
God will break the rod of Assyria, and Babylon's pride will fall like a bright morning star.
chapters.application: Pride is a great spiritual enemy; humility before God leads to true exaltation. May we stay watchful, never grow arrogant in a moment of success, and remember that God always deals justly.

chapters.summary: Isaiah announces the destruction of Moab, punished for its pride and arrogance, bringing weeping across the land and desolate cities.
keyPoints: Moab's cities are destroyed overnight; the people weep, shaving their heads and beards in mourning.
The Moabites flee to neighboring lands carrying their goods and provisions, but disaster still overtakes them.
The prophet weeps for Moab, for its vines and crops have withered, and wailing spreads across the whole land.
chapters.application: Pride brings a person down; only reliance on God gives true stability. When we see others suffer, let us respond with compassion, and examine whether we ourselves have drifted from God.

chapters.summary: Isaiah 16 continues the prophecy against Moab, declaring that disaster will come because of its pride, but also hinting at a future promise of grace and restoration.
keyPoints: Moab is urged to send tribute to Judah in search of refuge.
Because of its pride and arrogance, Moab suffers God's judgment and unending wailing.
Moab's destruction is foretold, yet there is a hint of hope for future restoration.
chapters.application: In times of ease, guard against self-reliant pride, and humbly rely on God instead, for he remembers the afflicted and gives mercy and hope.

chapters.summary: Isaiah prophesies judgment on Damascus and Israel, but promises that a remnant will turn back to God.
keyPoints: The city of Damascus will become a ruin, and the glory of Syria will fade.
Israel is judged for trusting in idols and foreign alliances, left like a harvested field with only a few gleanings.
A remnant will look to their Maker, no longer relying on false altars.
chapters.application: Let us examine what our hearts truly rely on, putting away every idol and turning back to the true God, for he is merciful and will preserve a remnant.

chapters.summary: Isaiah announces God's judgment and salvation concerning Cush (Ethiopia), showing that God rules over all nations and will in due time care for his own people.
keyPoints: Though Cush is powerful, God will judge them as one prunes away branches at harvest time.
All peoples are to bring gifts to the LORD of hosts, to Mount Zion.
God will visit his people at the appointed time, bringing them blessing.
chapters.application: Whatever the circumstances, trust in God's sovereignty; he will bring about justice and salvation in his own time, and we should wait for him with reverence.

chapters.summary: Isaiah prophesies that Egypt will fall into confusion under the LORD's judgment, but that in the end Egypt, Assyria, and Israel will worship the LORD together and become a blessed people.
keyPoints: The LORD rides on a swift cloud into Egypt, making Egypt's idols and hearts tremble.
Egypt's wise men and gods are powerless to help, and both its economy and the Nile are struck.
The Egyptians cry out to the LORD, and he answers and sends them a savior; Egypt, Assyria, and Israel will worship together, becoming a blessing to the world.
chapters.application: In times of trouble, do not rely on human wisdom or idols, but call earnestly on the LORD; he will hear and save, letting us experience his grace and unity even in hardship.

chapters.summary: Isaiah walks stripped and barefoot for three years as a living sign that Egypt and Cush will be carried off by Assyria, warning Judah not to trust in them.
keyPoints: In obedience to God's command, Isaiah goes stripped and barefoot for three years as an omen that Egypt and Cush will be taken captive by Assyria.
God declares that Egypt and Cush will be led away captive, putting to shame those who relied on them, and exposing the emptiness of trusting in man.
The people of Judah must realize that Egypt, in whom they trusted, is useless, and turn instead to trust in God, lest they suffer the same disgrace.
chapters.application: Do not rely on human strength and power; trust in God alone. Even when circumstances bring shame, God still reigns, and turning back to him brings true security.

chapters.summary: Isaiah announces God's judgment on Babylon, Edom, and Arabia, showing that God rules over all nations and calling people to turn to him.
keyPoints: Babylon will fall; the prophet, terrified by the vision, announces its fate.
Edom and Arabia also face judgment; those fleeing must escape the sword and disaster.
God reveals the destiny of the nations, showing his sovereignty and the certainty of his judgment.
chapters.application: The world's affairs are turbulent and uncertain, but God rules over all. Let us watch and pray, holding fast to faith amid change, and wait for his salvation.

chapters.summary: Isaiah announces that Jerusalem will be judged for relying on its own defenses instead of God, prophesies its fall, and points to Shebna's demotion and Eliakim's rise as a picture of the transfer of authority in the house of David.
keyPoints: Because Jerusalem is proud and trusts in its own weapons rather than looking to God, it will face siege and humiliation.
God calls the people to repentance, but instead they indulge in feasting and revelry, so their sin remains unforgiven.
Shebna is removed for his self-exaltation, and Eliakim is appointed a faithful steward, foreshadowing the authority of the Messiah.
chapters.application: When facing difficulty, we easily rely on our own devices, but God wants us to look to him. May we humbly repent, be faithful stewards, and give all glory to God.

chapters.summary: Isaiah announces the destruction of Tyre for its pride and greed, but prophesies its eventual restoration, and that its wealth will finally give glory to God.
keyPoints: Because of Tyre's arrogance and the sin bound up in its trade, God lays it waste, and the nations mourn.
Tyre's downfall ripples out to the coastal lands, including Egypt and Judah, showing the far reach of God's judgment.
After seventy years Tyre will be restored, but its wealth will ultimately belong to the LORD, offered in his worship.
chapters.application: Let us humbly rely on God rather than boast in wealth and achievement, knowing that everything ultimately belongs to him, and using what we have to glorify him.

chapters.summary: Isaiah 24 prophesies that God will judge the whole earth, laying it waste, yet a remnant will praise him, and in the end God will reign as king on Mount Zion.
keyPoints: God will make the earth empty and desolate, judging its inhabitants without regard to rank or status.
Because the inhabitants have broken the everlasting covenant and transgressed the law, the earth is cursed and its people grow few.
The remnant will shout for joy and praise God, for the LORD reigns on Mount Zion, displaying his glory.
chapters.application: Facing the injustice and corruption of the world, let us hold fast to faith, knowing that God will surely bring justice. Even in hardship, let us hope in his reign and live holy, God-fearing lives.

chapters.summary: Isaiah prophesies that after judging the nations, God will spread a rich feast for all peoples on Mount Zion, swallow up death, and bring salvation and joy.
keyPoints: The prophet praises God for accomplishing wonderful plans, turning a fortified city into ruins, showing his faithfulness.
God prepares a feast for all peoples, removes the veil that covers them, swallows up death, and wipes away tears from every face.
Moab's pride is foretold to be trampled down, while God's people rejoice in his salvation.
chapters.application: Facing hardship and sorrow in life, trust in God's promise for the last days: he will wipe away our tears and give us abundant grace, so that we rejoice in his salvation.

chapters.summary: This chapter expresses trust in God through praise and prayer, declaring his salvation and judgment, and encouraging the people to hold fast to him in hardship.
keyPoints: Judah will sing a song of salvation, for God gives them a strong city and keeps them safe.
God brings the proud low and lifts up the humble, revealing his righteousness.
Believers are to wait for God, for his judgment will surely come upon the wicked.
chapters.application: In hardship, hold fast to God with your whole heart, for he is the everlasting Rock. Wait quietly for his work, and you will find peace and deliverance.

chapters.summary: This chapter declares that God will punish evil powers, protect Israel like a vineyard, and gather his scattered people to return and worship him on his holy mountain.
keyPoints: With his fierce, great sword, God will punish Leviathan, the fleeing serpent, symbolizing the defeat of evil powers.
God watches over the vineyard, watering it every moment, showing his protection and care for his people.
Israel will one day take root and blossom, filling the whole world, as God gathers them back home.
chapters.application: Whatever our circumstances, God never stops caring for his people. Let us rely on him in faith, confident that he will keep us and lead us toward restoration.

chapters.summary: Isaiah warns against Ephraim's pride and drunkenness, declares that the LORD will judge with wonderful acts, promises that Zion will be redeemed, and teaches wisdom and righteousness.
keyPoints: Ephraim's leaders, made proud by drunkenness, are like a fading flower and will surely be judged.
Through wondrous acts, the LORD uses foreign nations to punish his rebellious people, revealing his justice.
Zion will be saved and become a sure foundation; whoever trusts in it will never be shaken.
chapters.application: Humbly rely on God rather than your own strength; he will be our sure foundation, giving peace and guidance even in hardship.

chapters.summary: Isaiah declares that Jerusalem will be judged for its empty worship and pride, but God will act wonderfully to save, giving understanding to the foolish.
keyPoints: Jerusalem builds altars and offers sacrifices, yet its heart is far from God, making its worship mere outward form.
God will judge Israel's blindness and pride, bringing them to shame.
After judgment, God will do a marvelous thing, bringing joy to the humble and understanding to the foolish.
chapters.application: Examine your own faith - has it become mere form? Turn back to God in humility, and he will give you wisdom and renewal.

chapters.summary: Isaiah warns Judah not to rely on Egypt but to rely on the LORD instead, and promises that God will show grace to those who wait for him.
keyPoints: Judah is rebuked for making an alliance with Egypt, trusting in human power rather than God's help.
Egypt's help is declared useless; only repentance and turning to God brings salvation.
God promises to bless those who wait for him, granting them guidance and abundance.
chapters.application: In hardship we often want to rely on human methods, but God wants us to turn and wait for him. He will show grace to those who wait, giving true peace and guidance.

chapters.summary: This chapter warns Judah not to depend on Egypt's military might but to depend on the LORD, and promises that God will protect Jerusalem, calling the people to turn back to him.
keyPoints: The LORD rebukes Judah for going down to Egypt for help without regard for the Holy One of Israel.
God himself will protect Jerusalem, hovering over it like a bird guarding its young, and will deliver them.
The people are called to turn back to God and cast away their idols, for he will forgive and save them.
chapters.application: When facing hardship we often want to rely on human strength, but God invites us to turn back to him. He will protect us as a mother bird shelters her young. Let us lay down our own schemes and look wholly to God's salvation.

chapters.summary: Isaiah prophesies that a righteous king will bring peace, warns the complacent women that disaster is coming, and promises that in the end the Spirit poured out will bring renewal.
keyPoints: A righteous king will reign, bringing justice and peace, like a shelter from the storm and streams of water.
The complacent women are warned to listen, for judgment is coming and the land will lie desolate.
After the Spirit is poured out, the wilderness will become a fruitful field, and righteousness and peace will fill the land.
chapters.application: Amid turmoil, let us build our lives on righteousness rather than seeking ease, look to the work of the Spirit, and trust that God will bring peace and renewal.

chapters.summary: This chapter announces God's judgment on oppressors, and promises that Zion will be kept safe in hardship, finally enjoying security and abundance.
keyPoints: God will judge the plunderers, and their plunder will come to nothing.
In distress, the righteous cry out to God, and he becomes their stronghold.
God will give Zion peace, filled with wisdom and righteousness.
chapters.application: Facing injustice and hardship, rely wholly on God; he watches over the righteous and gives peace and provision.

chapters.summary: God pronounces judgment on the nations, especially Edom, foreshadowing his righteous punishment and the restoration of Zion.
keyPoints: God summons all peoples to hear his judgment; the nations are destroyed, and even the heavens and their host are swept up in it.
Edom is punished for its enmity toward God; its land lies waste and becomes a haunt for wild creatures.
The judgment reveals God's righteousness; Zion will be saved, and his promises belong to his chosen people.
chapters.application: When you face injustice and evil, trust in God's righteousness. He will judge the wicked and keep those who belong to him, so stand firm in hope.

chapters.summary: Isaiah 35 pictures the restoration that follows God's salvation of his people: the wilderness becomes fruitful, the weak are made strong, and a Highway of Holiness is opened for the redeemed to return to Zion with joy.
keyPoints: The wilderness and the dry land will be glad, and the desert will blossom abundantly, displaying the glory of God.
Weak hands and feeble knees will be strengthened, and fearful hearts encouraged, for God himself is coming to bring vindication and salvation.
The blind, deaf, lame, and mute are healed, rivers flow in the desert, and God prepares a Highway of Holiness for the redeemed — the unclean shall not pass over it.
themes: The Highway of Holiness and the Return
chapters.application: When life feels as dry and weary as the wilderness, remember that God promises living water to heal our weakness. May we walk by faith on the highway he has prepared, singing for joy until we come into his presence.

chapters.summary: Assyria's King Sennacherib attacks Judah, and his field commander, the Rabshakeh, hurls arrogant threats at Jerusalem, trying to shake the people's faith in God.
keyPoints: The Assyrian army closes in, and the Rabshakeh terrorizes the people of Judah with threats of overwhelming force.
The Rabshakeh blasphemes God, claiming that the LORD cannot save Jerusalem.
Judah's officials say nothing in response, then tear their clothes and report the matter to Hezekiah.
chapters.application: When the world threatens us with intimidation and lies, let us follow the example of Judah's officials: instead of rushing to argue back, turn to God and seek his help and deliverance in prayer.

chapters.summary: As the Assyrian army lays siege, King Hezekiah seeks out Isaiah, and God promises deliverance through the prophet, then strikes down the Assyrian army, displaying his faithfulness and power.
keyPoints: Facing the Assyrian threat, Hezekiah humbly cries out to God and sends men to consult Isaiah.
Isaiah delivers God's word, prophesying that the Assyrian king will fall and the people will be delivered.
God sends his angel to strike down 185,000 men in the Assyrian camp, and Hezekiah is delivered.
chapters.application: When facing hardship, follow Hezekiah's example: seek God first, lay your burden before him, and trust that he will watch over you and give you a peace beyond understanding.

chapters.summary: King Hezekiah falls deathly ill and prays to God, who grants him fifteen more years of life and gives the sign of the shadow moving backward; Hezekiah then writes a psalm of thanksgiving.
keyPoints: Hezekiah, near death, weeps and prays, asking God to remember his faithfulness.
Through Isaiah, God promises to heal him and add fifteen years to his life.
The shadow moves back ten steps as a sign, and Hezekiah composes a psalm to give God thanks and praise.
chapters.application: In sickness or hardship, follow Hezekiah's example: pray earnestly, trust God's promises, and keep a thankful heart that bears witness to his grace and faithfulness.

chapters.summary: King Hezekiah shows off his wealth to envoys from Babylon; Isaiah prophesies that Judah will be carried into exile, yet Hezekiah is content as long as he himself has peace.
keyPoints: Envoys from Babylon visit, and Hezekiah displays all his treasures, revealing his pride.
Isaiah announces God's judgment: everything will be carried off to Babylon, and Hezekiah's descendants will become eunuchs there.
Hezekiah's response is that he is content, so long as there is peace in his own lifetime.
chapters.application: When life is going well, guard against pride. Keep a heart of gratitude and humility, thinking of future generations and God's kingdom purposes rather than only your own present comfort.

chapters.summary: Isaiah 40 declares that God comforts his people, prepares the way, reveals his glory and power, and encourages the people to wait on him.
keyPoints: God commands the prophet to comfort his people, announcing that their hard service is over and their sin has been pardoned.
A way is to be prepared for the LORD in the wilderness; every obstacle will be leveled, and the glory of God will be revealed.
God is a mighty shepherd whose understanding is unsearchable; those who wait on him will renew their strength.
chapters.application: In hardship, remember that God still reigns and gives strength to those who wait on him. Let us look to him in faith, renew our strength, and rise up on wings like eagles.

chapters.summary: Through Isaiah, God declares his sovereignty over the nations and encourages Israel not to fear, for he will help them.
keyPoints: God calls the coastlands and the peoples to be silent, showing that he governs history and has raised up Cyrus to accomplish his purposes.
God rebukes Israel for the uselessness of idols, insisting that he alone is the true God, who alone can declare things to come.
God comforts weak Israel, promising to give them strength and to make them into a threshing instrument.
chapters.application: When you face life's challenges, do not be afraid, for God has promised to be with you. He will uphold you with his righteous right hand and give you strength to overcome.

chapters.summary: Isaiah 42 declares that God's chosen Servant will bring justice and salvation; it calls the people to praise God and points to Israel's failure and God's discipline.
keyPoints: God's chosen Servant will bring forth justice with righteousness, gently leading the nations.
God, who created and sustains him, appoints his Servant as a covenant to the people and a light to the nations.
Though Israel is God's chosen people, they have rebelled, and God will discipline and save them through suffering.
chapters.application: In hardship, remember that God is our Creator, and he will sustain us. Let us answer his call in faith, becoming light in the world and bearing witness to his justice and salvation.

chapters.summary: God promises to redeem Israel, declares himself the one true God, and foretells that he will do a new thing to bring salvation to his people.
keyPoints: As their Creator, God comforts his chosen people, promising to be with them and to redeem them.
God is the only Savior; there is no salvation apart from him, and he condemns the emptiness of idols.
God declares that he is doing a new thing, making a way in the wilderness and rivers in the desert, displaying his glory.
chapters.application: Whatever your circumstances, remember that God has called you by name and will be with you. Do not be bound by the past; trust the new thing God is doing, and see his provision even in hardship.

chapters.summary: God promises to pour out his Spirit on Israel's descendants, insists that he is the one true God with no other Savior beside him, and exposes the emptiness of idols.
keyPoints: God reaffirms his choosing of Jacob, promising to pour out his Spirit on his offspring and bless their descendants.
God declares that he is the First and the Last, that there is no God besides him, and he exposes the falseness of idols.
God calls his people to remember these things, for he has redeemed Israel and will rebuild Jerusalem.
chapters.application: Remember that God alone is real; let us turn away from every idol and rely on him wholeheartedly, for he will redeem us and give us hope of restoration.

chapters.summary: God chooses Cyrus, king of Persia, as his instrument, revealing that he alone is the true God who governs all things, and he promises to save Israel.
keyPoints: God anoints Cyrus, subdues the nations before him, and levels the way for him to accomplish God's purpose.
God is the one true God; there is no salvation apart from him. He forms light and creates darkness, brings peace and creates calamity.
God's righteousness and salvation go together, and he calls all the ends of the earth to turn to him and be saved.
chapters.application: Entrust everything to God, for he governs history and the future. In hardship, trust his promises, and boldly bear witness to others that he alone is the Savior.

chapters.summary: God declares that he alone is the true God, far above Babylon's idols, and that he will accomplish his purpose and save Israel.
keyPoints: Babylon's idols are loaded onto beasts of burden, weighing them down, unable even to save themselves.
God has declared the end from the beginning; his purposes will surely stand.
God will save Israel, carrying them as he has done from the womb, even to their old age.
chapters.application: When we face pressure or temptation, remember that God alone reigns and his promises never fail. Simply trust him, and he will carry us to the very end.

chapters.summary: God pronounces judgment on Babylon: because of her pride and cruelty, she will fall from her throne, and no one will save her.
keyPoints: Babylon boasts of being eternal, but her arrogance and her oppression of God's chosen people bring down his punishment.
Though God once used Babylon to discipline Israel, Babylon's cruelty and self-exaltation bring about her own downfall.
Babylon's wisdom and sorceries cannot save her from disaster, exposing the emptiness of her idols.
chapters.application: Let us humbly depend on God rather than boast in our own power; he judges the proud and lifts up the lowly. Examine your heart today, turn away from self-satisfaction, and keep a spirit of gratitude and submission.

chapters.summary: God rebukes Israel's stubbornness, yet declares that for his own name's sake and his glory he will deliver them from Babylon, and he calls them to heed his ways.
keyPoints: God rebukes Israel for invoking his name with their lips while their hearts remain hardened and their deeds evil.
God foretells new things, demonstrating his sovereignty and foreknowledge.
For the sake of his own name, God withholds his judgment and shows his loving devotion through redemption.
chapters.application: Let us examine our hearts, lest we honor God with our lips while our hearts are far from him. Let us obey his leading, so that our peace may flow like a river and our righteousness like the waves of the sea.

chapters.summary: This chapter declares that God's Servant will be a light to the nations, bringing salvation, and comforts the exiles with the assurance that God will never forget them.
keyPoints: God chose his Servant from the womb, equipping him to restore Israel.
The Servant will not only restore Israel but will also be a light to the nations, bringing salvation to the ends of the earth.
God comforts the exiled people, promising their return, and assures them he will never forget them.
chapters.application: Whatever our circumstances, God remembers us, and his promises never fail. Let us wait in faith, for he will surely give salvation and comfort.

chapters.summary: Through the prophet Isaiah, God declares that he has not forsaken Israel; rather, he sends his Servant (who prefigures Christ) to suffer, calling the people to trust and obey.
keyPoints: God questions why Israel feels forsaken, showing that it is not he who has divorced them, but their own sin that has brought this upon them.
God has the power to save, yet he lets the people face the consequences of their own rebellion, while still promising salvation.
The Servant obeys God, enduring insult and beating, becoming an example and a hope for those who trust in him.
chapters.application: When we feel forsaken by God, let us examine whether our own sin has driven us from him. Let us learn from the obedience of the Servant, Jesus, relying on God in suffering rather than on our own strength.

chapters.summary: Isaiah 51 encourages the exiled people to remember Abraham, declares that God will save Zion, and calls them to look to God's righteousness and salvation.
keyPoints: Remember Abraham and Sarah — God will bless their descendants and comfort Zion.
God's righteousness and salvation are near, though the heavens and the earth will wear out like a garment.
Do not fear the reproach and slander of men, for God's salvation will last forever.
chapters.application: When we feel weak or afraid, let us look to the God who created the heavens and the earth; he will give us strength and peace.

chapters.summary: This chapter declares that Jerusalem will be freed from captivity, God will save his people, and all the nations will see his salvation.
keyPoints: Zion is called to awake and clothe herself with strength and splendor, for the holy city has been redeemed.
The people are redeemed freely, without money, by the power of God alone.
The Servant will be raised up high, and the nations will be astonished, for God has revealed his holy arm.
chapters.application: Whatever hardship we face, be assured that God will save. Wait in faith, for God has prepared salvation, and joyfully proclaim the good news of peace.

chapters.summary: This chapter prophesies the suffering Servant, the Messiah, who bears our iniquities — by his wounds we are healed.
keyPoints: The Servant is despised and rejected, a man of sorrows and acquainted with grief, one from whom people hide their faces.
Surely he has borne our griefs and carried our sorrows; the punishment that brought us peace was upon him.
It was the LORD's will to crush him and cause him to suffer, making his life a guilt offering; yet he will see his offspring and prolong his days.
chapters.application: When we are in affliction, let us remember that Christ has already borne the greatest suffering on our behalf. Because of this, we can find rest in his love, and learn to face life's trials with obedience and faith.

chapters.summary: This chapter declares the LORD's steadfast love and promise to Israel, like a husband to his wife — he will not cast her off, and he grants peace and an unshakable covenant.
keyPoints: The barren woman is called to sing, for the LORD will give her many descendants and enlarge her tent.
The LORD is Creator and Redeemer; though he was angry for a moment, he shows Israel everlasting love and compassion.
The mountains may depart and the hills be removed, but God's steadfast love and his covenant of peace will never be shaken.
chapters.application: When you feel forsaken or discouraged, remember that God loves you with an everlasting love and his promises do not change. Sing even in hardship, for he will enlarge your territory and give you peace.

chapters.summary: God invites everyone who thirsts to come and receive salvation, promising abundant grace and everlasting life, and calls people to seek him while he may be found.
keyPoints: God freely provides the water of life, with no need for money or labor.
God renews his covenant with David, promising that all nations will come to his Holy One.
Seek the LORD while he may be found; forsake your evil ways and turn to him.
chapters.application: Are you thirsty today? Come near to God, for he gives grace freely. Turn to him now — he will have mercy and pardon.

chapters.summary: Isaiah 56 calls the people to uphold justice and righteousness, declares that foreigners and eunuchs who keep God's covenant will also be accepted by him, and rebukes Israel's leaders for failing in their duty.
keyPoints: God calls his people to maintain justice and do what is right, for his salvation is near.
Eunuchs and foreigners who keep his covenant will be accepted by God.
Israel's leaders are rebuked as blind watchmen and mute dogs.
chapters.application: Whatever your background, if you fear God and hold to righteousness, you will be accepted by him. Be alert to failures in leadership, and be a faithful watchman yourself.

chapters.summary: This chapter rebukes Israel's idolatry and hypocrisy, while promising that God will heal, guide, and give peace to the humble and contrite.
keyPoints: The righteous perish, and are spared from the calamity to come, yet few understand that this, too, is God's mercy.
Israel has fallen into idolatry and spiritual adultery, even sacrificing their children, greatly offending God.
God promises to dwell with the humble and contrite, giving them life, peace, and healing.
chapters.application: Examine your heart for hidden idols, and humbly turn back to God. He will forgive, heal, and give you true peace.

chapters.summary: This chapter shows that true fasting is not outward self-affliction but doing justice and showing mercy, and promises blessing to those who obey.
keyPoints: It exposes hollow, outward religion and calls for genuine repentance.
True fasting is loosing the bonds of injustice and sharing bread with the hungry.
Those who do God's will are promised his guidance and provision.
chapters.application: Examine your spiritual life — is it focused only on outward form while neglecting mercy and justice? May we show love through action, and experience God's presence and guidance.

chapters.summary: This chapter shows that the people's sin has made God hide his face and refuse to hear, yet God himself will bring redemption and make a covenant with his people.
keyPoints: The LORD's arm is not too short to save; rather, it is your sins that have separated you from God.
The people's evil deeds are like a spider's web, unable to cover their sin; the mischief and lies they conceive will come back upon them.
Seeing that no one would intercede, God himself brought salvation with his own arm, putting on righteousness as a breastplate and salvation as a helmet.
chapters.application: When you feel your prayers are hindered, first examine whether you have drifted from God. God does not distance himself from us, but sin blocks our fellowship with him. Confess and repent, and trust in God's own salvation.

chapters.summary: This chapter prophesies Jerusalem's future glory, when the nations will come to her light, and describes her restoration and prosperity.
keyPoints: Jerusalem's light has come, and the nations will come to that light.
The wealth and resources of the nations will flow into the holy city, bringing prosperity.
The holy city will become a center of righteousness and praise, forever cared for by God.
chapters.application: When we are in darkness, let us look to God's light, believe that his promises will be fulfilled, and live out light and hope.

chapters.summary: Isaiah 61 declares that the Spirit of the LORD has anointed the prophet to bring salvation, comfort, joy, and righteousness, and prophesies Israel's restoration and the nations' witness of it.
keyPoints: The Spirit of the LORD anoints the prophet to bring good news to the humble, bind up the brokenhearted, and proclaim liberty to the captives.
He gives a crown of beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, a garment of praise for a spirit of despair, making his people oaks of righteousness.
Israel is called the priests of the LORD and his ministers; they will inherit a double portion, and God makes an everlasting covenant with them, giving them lasting joy.
chapters.application: When we are in hardship, let us trust that God can turn our sorrow into joy, and that he calls us to be channels of blessing to others, living out righteousness and glory.

chapters.summary: Isaiah declares that Jerusalem will be saved; God will give her a new name and appoint watchmen to pray day and night until her righteousness shines forth like the dawn.
keyPoints: God promises not to keep silent until Jerusalem's righteousness shines out like the dawn and her salvation like a burning lamp.
The nations will see God's glory, and Jerusalem will receive a new name, becoming the one in whom God delights.
Watchmen are appointed to cry out day and night, preparing the way and announcing that salvation has come; God himself will bring it to pass.
chapters.application: Pray persistently for God's promises, trusting that he will fulfill them. While you wait, declare his salvation in faith, and be a faithful watchman until his glory appears.

chapters.summary: Isaiah 63 portrays God as a warrior who judges his enemies and saves his people, and it looks back on his steadfast love and faithfulness throughout Israel's history.
keyPoints: God judges the nations in righteousness, vindicating his people.
The chapter recalls God's salvation and guidance during the exodus and the wilderness years.
Though the people rebelled, God still showed them love and compassion.
chapters.application: God's righteousness and love always go together; let us trust in his salvation and remember his grace in our daily lives, responding with a thankful heart.

chapters.summary: Isaiah pleads for the LORD to tear open the heavens and come down in power; he confesses the people's sin and uncleanness, yet cries out for mercy, for God is their Father and their Potter.
keyPoints: He begs God to display his power, tearing open the heavens and coming down so that the nations tremble.
He confesses that the people's righteous acts are like filthy rags, and that their sins are consuming them.
He pleads with God not to give them up, for he is their Father and their Potter, and asks him to show grace.
chapters.application: When our sin has driven us from God, let us follow Isaiah's example: humbly confess, and hold firmly to the truth that God is our loving Father, who will save us according to his mercy.

chapters.summary: God responds to those who seek him and promises a new heavens and a new earth, while those who rebel will face judgment.
keyPoints: God reveals himself to a people who did not seek him, while Israel is rejected because of their rebellion.
God promises that a remnant will inherit blessing, while the rebellious will be punished.
God will create new heavens and a new earth, bringing everlasting joy and peace.
themes: New Heavens and a New Earth
chapters.application: Let us actively seek God, for he delights to draw near to us; at the same time, let us hold to holiness, for God will judge in righteousness, and he will also give us everlasting hope.

chapters.summary: The final chapter of Isaiah declares God's judgment on all peoples and promises the glory of all nations worshiping in the new heavens and new earth.
keyPoints: God looks with favor on the humble and contrite in spirit, not on empty religious ritual.
As a mother comforts her child, so God will comfort his people, with Jerusalem as that comforting mother.
All nations and peoples will be gathered to see God's glory; the wicked will be punished, but the righteous will endure forever.
chapters.application: Examine your spiritual life: does it emphasize inner humility and obedience rather than outward form? In hardship, look to God's comfort, and hold on to the hope of the new heavens and new earth.
